cv_heading: Selected artistic and cultural work presented to the public
title: Museum of Quietness
venue: THEMUSEUM, Kitchener, Ontario — presented within "SONICA – A Sound Experience"
description: A participatory art experience inviting audiences to examine the auditory and visual noise in their surroundings, then design their own artifacts imagining a quieter future and their role in creating it. Presented in person at THEMUSEUM and virtually over Zoom for pandemic-isolated participants.

cv_heading: Selected artistic and cultural work presented to the public
title: One Day They Will Return
description: A speculative fiction project imagining a world where birds mysteriously vanish, prompting humanity to build elaborate nests decorated with bird memorabilia in hopes of their return — exploring environmental collapse, collective denial, and humanity's attempts to restore what has been lost through sculptural installations, sonic environments, and immersive storytelling.

cv_heading: Selected artistic and cultural work presented to the public
title: Wishing Well
description: A participatory soundscape and live sonification work. Materials: borrowed objects from local shops, reclaimed roof tiles from the Hsinchu City Railway Warehouse, contact mics, and a bio-sonification module. Sound design by Luisa Ji and Benjamin Lappalainen; production support from Husna Farooqui.

cv_heading: Selected artistic and cultural work presented to the public
title: Sediments
venue: Residency: DAÏMÔN / Radio-Hull; Performance: Place-des-artistes de Farrellton
description: Environmental sonification and collected soundscapes derived from local ecosystems near Wakefield, Quebec. Performed with Hooria Rahimi at River Room, a spatial installation by Rahimi.

cv_heading: Selected artistic and cultural work presented to the public
title: When Spiders Spin Dusk
venue: Research and Creation: June–September 2024, residency at Ferme Lanthorn, Wakefield, Quebec; Exhibitions: Toronto 2024 (The Bridge), Seoul 2025 (Coréana Museum of Art, Space*c)
description:
An exhibition at [Carnival of Shipwreck](/cultural-production/carnival-of-shipwreck.html) (Toronto, October 22–26, 2024), developed through [Intelligent Terrain](/programs/intelligent-terrain.html)'s 2024 Canada–Korea residency at Ferme Lanthorn, and shown in Seoul in 2025.

Six artists based in Canada and Korea jointly researched and developed works on geological shifts, cultural perspectives on AI, and technology's relationship to the more-than-human world: SunJeong Hwang, Unmake Lab, Sunjoo Lee, Maurice Jones, François Quévillon and Erika Jean Lincoln. An international co-production with Junghyun Kim, funded by the Canada Council for the Arts and Arts Council Korea.

[Read the curatorial statement](/writing/when-spiders-spin-dusk-statement.html)

cv_heading: Selected artistic and cultural work presented to the public
title: Shipwreck
description: A durational presentation format centring on the question of "how do we make a home among ruins?"

cv_heading: Selected artistic and cultural work presented to the public
title: Carnival of Shipwreck
venue: The Bridge (379 Adelaide St. W.) and Spadinababy (688 Richmond St. W.), Toronto
description:
A five-day festival of provocations, performances, installations, workshops, music and dancing, presented by UKAI Projects (Kasra Goodarznezhad, Jerrold McGrath and Luisa Ji). It takes up José Ortega y Gasset's idea that life is shipwreck and culture the swimming stroke that keeps us afloat: a chance to practise being in the storm and being in the water.

Exhibitions and special collaboration:

- [When Spiders Spin Dusk](/cultural-production/when-spiders-spin-dusk.html), curated by Junghyun Kim and UKAI Projects, at The Bridge
- Static Smirk: Frequencies of Embodiment through Dead Tech, curated by Chiedza Pasipanodya in collaboration with UKAI Projects, at Spadinababy
- The Feast II — The Shipwreck Came and Swept, curated by Shima, at Spadinababy

Five days of workshops and performance lectures, including Luisa Ji's workshop Make Your Own Wasteland, and music nights at both venues.

Photography: Nick Gallarza.
